sections.h2: Where does a Wayne County deed get recorded?
sections.html:
Wayne County deeds are recorded at the Recorder's Office on the first floor of the Administration Building, 428 West Liberty Street, Wooster, OH 44691. The phone number is 330-287-5460. The county describes the Recorder as the official who protects legal documents, most of them tied to real estate: deeds, mortgages and liens. All subdivision plats are filed there too.

The same building houses the Auditor, the Treasurer, the Board of Revision and the Map Office, so a deed can move from desk to desk without leaving the property. Wooster is the county seat of a county of about 555 square miles, formed by 1808 legislation and organized in 1812, and its 2025 estimated population is 116,758.

sections.h2: What route does a Wayne County deed follow before it is recorded?
sections.html:
The Auditor's real estate page lays out a fixed order. Skipping a step usually means the Recorder sends the paper back.

  • Prepare the deed, then bring it to the Map Office in the Administration Building.
  • Take it to the Auditor, who collects the conveyance fee and the transfer fee.
  • Carry the endorsed deed to the Recorder, where it is legally recorded.

Ohio's statement of value rule sits behind the Auditor's step. Under R.C. 319.202, the grantee files a statement declaring the value conveyed before the Auditor endorses the deed, and the grantor pays the conveyance fee. If the sale is exempt, the statement gives the reason for the exemption instead. The Auditor's forms library carries the exemption statement, DTE 100(EX).

sections.h2: What does the Wayne County Auditor charge at the conveyance step?
sections.html:
The Auditor's page prints a conveyance fee of $4.00 per thousand of the sale price, plus a transfer fee of $0.50 per parcel. It adds that the office rounds the sale price up to the next $100 before applying the rate. The Auditor also posts a Conveyance Fee Calculator under its Tools menu, which is the quickest way to see the charge for a particular price.

The Wayne County Treasurer has a role as well. A parcel with unpaid taxes can hold up a closing, so ask the Treasurer at 330-287-5450 for a payoff figure, and review the delinquent list on the Treasurer's site. The Auditor can be reached at 330-287-5430, Monday through Friday, 8:00 am to 4:30 pm.

sections.h2: How much does the Wayne County Recorder charge for recording?
sections.html:
The Auditor's page lists the recording fees below. They track the statute, R.C. 317.32, which sets $17 base plus $17 housing trust fund for the first two pages and $4 plus $4 for every later page. The statute also lets a county add a document preservation surcharge of up to $5, so ask the Recorder whether the current total includes it.

Recording charges printed on the Wayne County Auditor's Real Estate Property page
ItemCharge
First two pages$34.00
Each additional page$8.00
Marginal notation$4.00
Copies$2.00
Standardization guideline fee$20.00

The $20.00 line is the penalty for a document that fails the state's page format rules in R.C. 317.114. Check margins and ink with the Recorder before you sign.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Wayne County homes?
sections.html:
QuickFacts shows a county where roughly three of four homes are owner occupied, at 76.6 percent for 2020 to 2024. There are 44,365 households and 47,538 housing units, with 2.53 people per household.

  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $222,100.
  • Median gross rent: $881 a month.
  • Median household income: $73,574 in 2024 dollars.
  • Persons living in the same house a year earlier: 90.2 percent.
  • Building permits in 2025: 232.

With 90.2 percent of residents in the same house a year earlier, turnover is modest, and each recorded deed lands in a county of about 59,000 parcels, the count the Auditor's home page gives.

sections.h2: What should a seller bring to the Wayne County Recorder?
sections.html:
Bring the original deed with the Auditor's endorsement, a legal description that matches the prior deed, parcel numbers, and a check for the recording fee. The Treasurer's FAQ notes that some name changes call for a new deed, so check how the owner's name appears on the Auditor's parcel record.

  • The Recorder takes deeds, mortgages, liens and plats, and indexes them in the county's land records.
  • A mortgage release or satisfaction is a separate recording with its own marginal reference charge.
  • The Map Office is the first stop in the Auditor's own route, so check your parcel description there before you draft.

The Wayne County Auditor's website also offers a parcel search and a GIS parcel viewer, which show prior owners, acreage and last sale before you draft the deed.

sections.h2: What does the statement of value cover in a Wayne County sale?
sections.html:
The value on the statement is the full consideration paid or to be paid for the real estate, and R.C. 319.202 says that figure includes the amount of any mortgage or vendor's lien on the property. For a gift in whole or part, the value is the estimated open market price between a willing seller and a willing buyer. No one may willfully falsify the value.

The statement carries two disclosures. One asks whether the property's taxes will be reduced by the owner-occupied credit or homestead program, and the other asks whether the land was in agricultural use valuation and could face recoupment. In both cases the grantor and the grantee confirm they have accounted for the amount. A seller who knows the parcel carried a reduction should say so when the deed is prepared.

sections.h2: How do Wayne County tax dates affect a deed that closes near a due date?
sections.html:
Taxes are billed in two installments, with first half bills issued in January or February and second half bills in June or July. The Treasurer's 2026 due dates were February 26 and July 30. A 10 percent penalty applies after the due date, and half of it is returned if payment arrives within 10 days.

A deed that is recorded the same week a bill falls due needs a clear agreement about who pays. Bank due dates fall earlier than the Treasurer's, in 2026 on February 2 and July 13, which matters when a closing agent pays through a bank. The Treasurer takes partial payments toward the upcoming bill, and all of them are applied to that bill.

sections.h2: Which Wayne County offices should a seller phone?
sections.html:
• Recorder, 330-287-5460: deeds, mortgages, liens and plats.
  • Auditor, 330-287-5430: conveyance fee, forms, parcel records, Monday to Friday 8:00 am to 4:30 pm.
  • Treasurer, 330-287-5450: balances, receipts and payment by card or e-check.
  • Board of Revision, 330-287-5433: valuation complaints, filed January 1 through March 31.

All four are at 428 West Liberty Street in Wooster.

faqs.q: Where is the Wayne County Recorder's Office?
faqs.a: On the first floor of the Administration Building at 428 West Liberty Street in Wooster, phone 330-287-5460. The Auditor, Treasurer and Board of Revision work from the same address.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Wayne County?
faqs.a: The Auditor's page prints $34.00 for the first two pages and $8.00 for each added page, plus $4.00 for a marginal notation and a $20.00 standardization guideline fee. State law allows a preservation surcharge of up to $5, so confirm the total with the Recorder.

faqs.q: What is the Wayne County deed transfer fee?
faqs.a: The Auditor charges a $4.00 per thousand conveyance fee on the sale price, rounded up to the next $100, and a $0.50 transfer fee per parcel. The grantor pays the conveyance fee under state law.

faqs.q: Do I visit the Auditor before the Recorder in Wayne County?
faqs.a: Yes. The Auditor's page sends a deed to the Map Office, then the Auditor for the conveyance and transfer fees, then the Recorder for recording.

faqs.q: Who should I ask about my Wayne County property tax balance before closing?
faqs.a: Ask the Treasurer at 330-287-5450. The Treasurer's site also carries a delinquent list.
